blocks.note: Verdict: the application itself is sound; what blocks go-live is how production is set up. AR-03 is solved by the production compose files, AR-01 by a promotion script, and AR-02 and AR-04 need a decision (which database instance; a hostname and TLS).

blocks.p: React SPA served by Nginx on the frontend host; FastAPI API and an APScheduler worker on the backend host; ApsaraDB PostgreSQL 18. The worker pulls LSEG DataScope prices daily, computes ~170 derived series, refreshes CFTC, the event calendar (Claude with web search) and four Google-Sheet sources; the API serves charts, intelligence pages and the admin console. Sign-in: local accounts and DWS Hub OIDC (PKCE).

blocks.p: **AR-01 - Production from a copy of staging**

Evidence and impact: Staging started in demo mode before its LSEG credentials were set, so synthetic rows may remain for instruments or dates the LSEG backfill did not overwrite; the worker never backfills a non-empty table and the first live run switches the demo banner off. The copy also carries valid staging sessions, OIDC states, users bound to the staging Hub's subjects, the Google key encrypted with the staging APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, staging jobs and an immutable staging audit trail.

Recommendation: Write and rehearse a promotion script (part of the production kit): delete price_daily where source = demo and recompute; truncate sessions, OIDC states and jobs; reset hub_sub so users re-bind by verified e-mail; keep the encryption key on purpose or re-enter the Google key; decide what happens to the audit log.
**AR-02 - Database roles on a shared instance**
Evidence and impact: bootstrap_roles.sql creates aastar_owner/app/ro and database aastar, and every migration grants to those literal names. Roles are instance-wide.

Recommendation: If production shares the staging instance: parameterise the names (or use group roles) first. If it shares another app's instance: check that no aastar_* role or aastar database exists there (the production preflight will).
Evidence and impact: The staging compose files declare no network; Docker's default pool includes 172.28.0.0/16, the hosts' own LAN, and the 172.30 range that holds the NAS.
Recommendation: The production compose files pin a subnet from the preflight with no default value.
Evidence and impact: Secure is set only for https. Browsers scope cookies by host, not port, so on http://172.28.80.50:3170 the session cookie would also reach every other app on that IP.
Recommendation: Give the app its own hostname through the host nginx from day one (even over HTTP this isolates the cookie), and move to HTTPS as soon as a certificate is available.

bullets: Formulas protected by golden tests against the legacy code, plus parity tests for every Google-Sheet source.
Clean layering: pure engine, bulk SQL in one store, thin routes, one Claude gateway, catalog as code synced by an idempotent bootstrap.
Efficient writes (COPY into temp tables, change-only upserts) and writers that cannot delete each other's points.
Sound concurrency: advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED job claims, one running pipeline run, job de-duplication, start-up recovery.

Security fundamentals: Argon2id with timing equalisation and lockout, hashed server-side sessions, CSRF double-submit plus Origin, per-series module checks, OIDC with PKCE S256 and JWKS, strict CSP without CDNs.
Audit trail written in the same transaction as the change and protected from the app role; JSON logs with request ids end to end.

blocks.p: **Before go-live:** AR-01 promotion script, AR-02 instance decision and check, AR-03 pinned subnet, AR-04 hostname (TLS when possible), AR-11/12/13/14 in the production kit (secrets file 600, sslmode=require, limits, backup before migrating), AR-15 production guide.
**After go-live:** AR-06 alerting and freshness, AR-10 CI, AR-16 job timeouts, AR-17 retention, AR-19 query fan-out, AR-23/24/25/27/28 hardening and tooling.
